text:
From fifteen to twenty she is a girl; a fine lass from twenty to twenty-five, and by the reckoning a gracious woman from twenty-five to thirty. Happy he who enjoys her at such an age!

From thirty to thirty-five she brings no joy; but may be eaten with salt and pepper; yet from thirty-five to forty she is already on the eve of disgrace.

At forty-five she is a learned scold, speaks through her nose, begs and toys with words; and once fifty is reached, she turns holy,

and at fifty-five sets up her shrine. Girl, lass, woman, crone, enchantress, witch and holy woman—the devil carries her off.

translation.title: On the Ages of Women
